source.title: Generalization at the Edge of Stability
source.authors: M. Tuci; Caner Korkmaz; Umut Simsekli; Tolga Birdal

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Reports training accuracy for MLPs on MNIST and modular arithmetic tasks, extending the training-fit finding to new settings; it does not test the listed CIFAR experiments or recipes.
record.gate_note: The paper reports training accuracy above 90% and reaching 100% early for its grokking evaluations. Other training-error values are not stated. Correlations between complexity measures and generalization gaps do not measure the claimed training-error behavior. Cited results are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study uses edge-of-stability training to develop and evaluate generalization measures. Its own results do not measure V5's loss recovery or full-batch sharpness-and-loss trajectories. R1 reports perfect training accuracy for a GELU MLP, whereas V1 names convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/100.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the empirical conclusion. The authors additionally derive a worst-case generalization bound over a random pullback attractor under stated regularity assumptions, linking the bound to Sharpness Dimension.
record.recipe_differences: The reported fit result uses a 2-layer GELU MLP on modular arithmetic, trained with SGD with momentum and weight decay; it does not use the cited CIFAR convolutional-network recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper varies learning rate, weight decay and seed across grokking evaluations, but does not report separate training-accuracy outcomes for these conditions.

fits_no_version.finding: The two-layer GELU MLP reaches 100% training accuracy early in the modular-addition evaluations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SGD with momentum and weight decay can achieve zero training classification error for a small GELU MLP on modular addition.

fits_no_version.finding: Sharpness Dimension predicts generalization gaps and tracks grokking transitions; the study also presents Hessian spectral estimates.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Full-spectrum measures of expansion and contraction can predict generalization in the tested optimization settings.

record.problems: The training-accuracy result is reported as an aggregate across evaluations, without separate values or uncertainty. The experiments use MNIST and modular arithmetic, not the CIFAR settings in V1.
record.rows_left_out: No other explicit training-accuracy result is stated. The paper's generalization-gap correlations and figure-only metric trajectories do not report the claimed training-error outcome.

untested.parts: Training fit of convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/100, including random labels and effects of model size, early stopping and regularization.
Teacher-student ReLU local minima and their reduction through extra student neurons.
Training degradation with depth and its prevention through identity shortcuts or special initialization.
Effects of initialization on training speed, signal propagation and trainable depth.
Loss recovery above the initial stability limit, divergence at larger rates, and full-batch sharpness hovering at the threshold while training loss falls.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparison with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The introduction's decreasing-loss and stability-threshold observations are attributed to prior studies. The conditional attractor and generalization theory does not independently demonstrate V5's training dynamics. Neither generalization-gap correlations nor transformed Hessian spectra establish those dynamics.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, convolutional networks, corrupted or random labels, comparisons by width, early stopping and other regularized recipes.

rows.subject: 2-layer MLP
rows.operation_detail: Trained with SGD with momentum and weight decay for 20k epochs on the modular arithmetic task.
rows.note: Aggregate statement covering all evaluations presented in Fig. 4; the text does not give separate training-accuracy values by learning rate, weight decay or seed.
rows.check: The reported training accuracy is correctly extracted, but the system and task do not match V1: this is a two-layer GELU MLP on modular addition, not a convolutional network on CIFAR-10/100. The result therefore cannot establish V1; its accuracy result itself is observed.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: The paper's modular arithmetic grokking evaluations
reader_labels.reason: Training accuracy exceeds 90% and reaches 100% early (R1), showing gradient training can reach zero training classification error in this setting.
